title: Bridgeback prioritization metalayer for escalated customer asks
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: VIP top-account escalations and ad-hoc product asks are currently routed ad hoc between AMs, SEs, and PMs. This creates unclear expectations, duplicated work, and missed SLAs for strategic customers. Goal: define a thin prioritization 'metalayer' that sits between intake (sales/AM/CS) and roadmap lanes. The metalayer will score escalated asks, assign a commitment SLA class, and output an explicit decision and handoff: Accept (with ETA and scope guardrails), Defer (with rationale and resourcing window), or Escalate-to-Exec (requires cross-functional approval). This ticket scopes the PM-side design, scoring rules, dashboards, and the initial canary rollout for top 15 accounts.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Prioritization engine design document approved by PM, Eng lead, and Head of CS. 2) Scoring rubric implemented as a service (mock mode) that returns score, top factors, and recommended SLA tier. 3) Console view shows pending escalations, score breakdown, and suggested decision; PMs can override and capture reason. 4) Runbook for SLA commitment windows (Accept/Defer/Escalate) published. 5) Pilot with 10 customer escalations completed and decision telemetry captured.
success_metrics: - Time-to-decision for escalations reduced from median 14 days to <=72 hours for P0s. - Acceptance precision: >=70% of accepted asks lead to a viable scoped follow-up epic within 4 sprints. - Reduction in duplicate engagements between AM/SE by 40% as measured by linked Github PRs and duplicate JIRA tickets. - Stakeholder satisfaction (post-pilot survey) >=4.0/5.
implementation_notes: Proposed components: (a) Intake hooks: Slack form + CS portal + email->ticket parser. (b) Scoring microservice (initial rule-based with weights for deal size, renewal proximity, legal/regulatory risk, technical dependency, strategic fit to OKRs). (c) Console UI: single table with filters and per-issue decision modal. (d) Audit log persisted to customer-audit store. Engineering will scope a mock mode first (no writes) to evaluate scoring signals. We will reuse existing analytics events and the Console Decision modal pattern from the Rollouts project.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (mock mode) weeks 1-2: deploy scoring service in mock mode, integrate with CS intake, collect 30 sample escalations. Phase 2 (soft accept) weeks 3-4: enable write-only decisions for PMs for 5 pilot accounts, document commitment SLAs. Phase 3 (pilot) weeks 5-8: full decision lifecycle for top 15 accounts, measure metrics and refine weights. Phase 4: broader launch and inclusion in 2025 Q2 roadmap intake process. Communication: cross-functional kickoff doc + weekly sync + final retrospective.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: scoring biases underestimate cross-functional effort -> Mitigation: include manual override and require PM rationale fields; track override rate. Risk: Customers expect immediate delivery after 'Accept' decision -> Mitigation: Accept must attach a templated commitment window and scope guardrails; legal/contract triggers flagged. Risk: Excess noise from low-signal escalations -> Mitigation: initial intake triage by CS with automated filters (renewal <90d, ARR threshold).
notes_from_design_review: Design session 2025-02-17 with Claire Nguyen and Mateo Ruiz. Feedback: surface top three contributing signals on the decision modal, keep default weight conservative for 'strategic fit' to avoid gaming. Design asked for 'reason templates' to speed PM responses. Action: add a lightweight composer and templated follow-ups.
engineering_feedback: ENG sync 2025-02-21: Eng requests to start with a rule-based service and telemetry endpoints; prefer to add ML-based re-ranking in a later release. Key dependency: data access to ARR/contract dates from SalesOps (blocker until ENG-1987 is resolved). Estimated backend work: 2 sprints for mock mode, +3 sprints for write path and audit logs.
product_decision_log: 2025-02-25: Agreed to 3-tier SLA (Immediate: <=72h decision, Near-term: 2-6 weeks, Defer: >6 weeks) and to limit pilot to top 15 revenue accounts. 2025-03-01: Decided to keep scoring explainable and rule-based for initial rollout.
